steps.instruction: Run 'make -f Makefile.ai ai-test' to start the test suite.
Check the test results in 'last-test.log'.
If a test fails, review the error and rerun with 'make -f Makefile.ai ai-test PYTEST_ARGS="-x"'.
Clone the repository and install dependencies.
Start the dev environment with 'make dev-up'.
Run 'make lint' to check code style.

Access the API documentation at the provided URL (e.g., http://localhost:9103/docs or your production API endpoint). If you are unsure of the correct URL, check your onboarding email or ask your project admin.

Generate your API token by sending a POST request to /admin/generate-token. For the first user token, no authentication is required. After the first token, an admin token is required to generate additional tokens.
Sample curl command to generate a user token (replace <api_url> as needed):

curl -X POST <api_url>/admin/generate-token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"description": "My first user token", "role": "user"}'
The response will include your new token. Save it securely! After the first token is created, you must include an admin token in the Authorization header to generate more tokens.
Once you have your token, add 'Authorization: Bearer <your_token>' to your API request headers. Your token will look like a long string of letters and numbers.
Try making your first API call! For example, to add a memory node, use the following command (replace <your_token> and <api_url> as needed):

curl -X POST <api_url>/memory/nodes \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your_token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"namespace": "external", "content": "Hello from the outside!", "meta": "{\"tags\":[\"external\"]}"}'
A successful response will return your new memory node as JSON. If you get a 401 error, check your token. If you get a 404, check the endpoint URL.
If you run into trouble, check the troubleshooting section in the docs or use the support resources linked there.
Start the dev environment:
make dev-up
Check that the API and memory endpoints are running. Visit http://localhost:9103/docs and look for /memory/nodes endpoints.

Add your first memory node (using curl): curl -X POST http://localhost:9103/memory/nodes -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"namespace": "onboarding", "content": "My first memory node!", "meta": "{\"tags\":[\"onboarding\"]}"}'
Or use the API docs 'Try it out' button.
Verify your memory node exists: curl http://localhost:9103/memory/nodes?namespace=onboarding | jq .
If you don't have jq installed, you can just run: curl http://localhost:9103/memory/nodes?namespace=onboarding
(Optional) Explore more: Try adding an edge, searching, or traversing the memory graph (see the Memory System Guide for examples).
Celebrate your achievement: Add an entry to the Pirate's Log (PIRATES_LOG.md) sharing your success!

paths.description: Set up your project to use the AI IDE API as a hosted memory (vector) server.

steps.title: Get Your API Key
steps.description: Contact your admin or use the /onboarding/init endpoint to obtain an API key.

steps.title: Create a Namespace
steps.description: Decide on a unique namespace for your project (e.g., your-project-name).

steps.title: Store and Search Memory
steps.description: Use the /memory/nodes and /memory/search endpoints to store and retrieve memory vectors. See the downloadable quickstart script for examples.
